stem:
A sphere of radius 10 cm carries a charge of \( 1\,\mu\text{C} \). Calculate the electric field
(i) at a distance of 30 cm from the center of the sphere
(ii) at the surface of the sphere and
(iii) at a distance of 5 cm from the center of the sphere.
solution:
Given: \( q = 1\,\mu\text{C} = 1 \times 10^{-6} \) C

(i) Electric intensity at a distance \( r \) is
\( E = q/4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2 \)
For \( r = 30 \) cm \( = 0.3 \) m
\( E = \dfrac{9 \times 10^{9} \times 1 \times 10^{-6}}{(0.3)^2} = 10^{5} \) N/C

(ii) \( E \) on the surface of the sphere, \( R = 10 \) cm \( = 0.10 \) m
\( E = q/4\pi\varepsilon_0 R^2 \)
\( = \dfrac{9 \times 10^{9} \times 1 \times 10^{-6}}{(0.10)^2} = 9 \times 10^{5} \) N/C

(iii) \( E \) at a point 5 cm away from the centre i.e. inside the sphere \( E = 0 \).

stem:
The length of a straight thin wire is 2 m. It is uniformly charged with a positive charge of \( 3\,\mu\text{C} \). Calculate
(i) the charge density of the wire
(ii) the electric intensity due to the wire at a point 1.5 m away from the center of the wire
solution:
Given
charge \( q = 3\,\mu\text{C} = 3 \times 10^{-6} \) C
Length \( l = 2 \) m, \( r = 1.5 \) m

(i) Charge Density \( \lambda = \) Charge/length
\( = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{-6}}{2} = 1.5 \times 10^{-6} \) C m\( ^{-1} \)

(ii) Electric Intensity \( E = \lambda / 2\pi\varepsilon_0 r \)
\( = \dfrac{1.5 \times 10^{-6}}{2 \times 3.142 \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 1.5} \)
\( = 1.798 \times 10^{4} \) N C\( ^{-1} \)

stem: The charge per unit area of a large flat sheet of charge is \( 3\,\mu\text{C/m}^2 \). Calculate the electric field intensity at a point just near the surface of the sheet, measured from its midpoint.
solution:
Given
Surface Charge Density \( = \sigma = 3 \times 10^{-6} \) Cm\( ^{-2} \)
Electric Intensity \( E = \sigma / 2\varepsilon_0 \)
\( = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{-6}}{2 \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12}} = 1.695 \times 10^{5} \) N C\( ^{-1} \)

stem:
Potential at a point A in space is given as \( 4 \times 10^{5} \) V.
(i) Find the work done in bringing a charge of \( 3\,\mu\text{C} \) from infinity to the point A.
(ii) Does the answer depend on the path along which the charge is brought?
solution:
Given
Potential \( (V) \) at the point A \( = 4 \times 10^{5} \) V
Charge \( q_0 = 3\,\mu\text{C} = 3 \times 10^{-6} \) C

(i) Work done in bringing the charge from infinity to the point A is
\( W_{\infty} = q_0 V \)
\( = 3 \times 10^{-6} \times 4 \times 10^{5} \)
\( = 12 \times 10^{-1} \)
\( W_{\infty} = 1.2 \) J

(ii) No, the work done is independent of the path.

A short electric dipole has dipole moment of \( 1 \times 10^{-9} \) C m. Determine the electric potential due to the dipole at a point distance 0.3 m from the centre of the dipole situated
a) on the axial line b) on the equatorial line c) on a line making an angle of \( 60^\circ \) with the dipole axis.
solution:
Given
\( p = 1 \times 10^{-9} \) Cm
\( r = 0.3 \) m

a) Potential at a point on the axial line
\( V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{p}{r^2} = \dfrac{9 \times 10^{9} \times 1 \times 10^{-9}}{(0.3)^2} = 100 \) volt

b) Potential at a point on the equatorial line \( = 0 \)

c) Potential at a point on a line making an angle of \( 60^\circ \) with the dipole axis is
\( V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{p\cos\theta}{r^2} = \dfrac{9 \times 10^{9} \times 1 \times 10^{-9}\cos 60^\circ}{(0.3)^2} \)
\( = 50 \) volt

stem: Two charges \( 5 \times 10^{-8} \) C and \( -3 \times 10^{-8} \) C are located 16 cm apart. At what point(s) on the line joining the two charges is the electric potential zero? Take the potential at infinity to be zero.
solution:
As shown below, suppose the two point charges are placed on \( x \)-axis with the positive charge located at the origin O.

\( q_1 = 5 \times 10^{-8} \) C at O, \( q_2 = -3 \times 10^{-8} \) C at A, with P between them; \( \text{OP} = x \), \( \text{PA} = 0.16 - x \), \( \text{OA} = 0.16 \) m.

Let the potential be zero at the point P and \( \text{OP} = x \). For \( x < 0 \) (i.e. to the left of O), the potentials of the two charges cannot add up to zero. Clearly, \( x \) must be positive. If \( x \) lies between O and A, then \( V_1 + V_2 = 0 \), where \( V_1 \) and \( V_2 \) are the potentials at point P due to O and A, respectively. The other possibility is that \( x \) may also lie on extended OA.

\( q_1 = 5 \times 10^{-8} \) C at O, \( q_2 = -3 \times 10^{-8} \) C at A, with P beyond A; \( \text{OA} = 0.16 \) m, \( \text{AP} = (x - 0.16) \) m.

\( \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left[\dfrac{q_1}{x} + \dfrac{q_2}{0.16 - x}\right] = 0 \)

\( 9 \times 10^{9}\left[\dfrac{5 \times 10^{-8}}{x} - \dfrac{3 \times 10^{-8}}{0.16 - x}\right] = 0 \)

\( \Rightarrow 9 \times 10^{9} \times 10^{-8}\left[\dfrac{5}{x} - \dfrac{3}{0.16 - x}\right] = 0 \)

\( \Rightarrow \dfrac{5}{x} - \dfrac{3}{0.16 - x} = 0 \)

\( \therefore x = 0.10 \) m

stem: A small particle carrying a negative charge of \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \) C is suspended in equilibrium between two horizontal metal plates 10 cm apart having a potential difference of 4000 \( V \) across them. Find the mass of the charged particle.
solution:
Given :
\( q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \) C
\( \mathrm{d}x = 10 \) cm \( = 10 \times 10^{-2} \) m \( = 10^{-1} \) m
\( \mathrm{d}V = 4000\ V \)

\( E = \dfrac{-\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{-4000}{10^{-1}} = -4 \times 10^{4} \) Vm\( ^{-1} \)

As the charged particle remains suspended in equilibrium,
\( F = mg = qE \)

\( \therefore m = \dfrac{qE}{g} = \dfrac{\left(-1.6 \times 10^{-19}\right)\left(-4 \times 10^{4}\right)}{9.8} \)

\( = 0.653 \times 10^{-15} \) kg

\( m = 6.53 \times 10^{-16} \) kg

subtopic: Potential Energy of Charges and Dipoles
stem: Calculate the electrostatic potential energy of the system of charges shown in the figure.
solution:
Taking zero of potential energy at \( \infty \), we get potential energy (PE) of the system of charges

\( \text{PE} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum \dfrac{q_j q_k}{r_{jk}} \)

\( = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left[\dfrac{q\,q}{r} + \dfrac{q(-q)}{r} + \dfrac{(-q)(-q)}{r} + \dfrac{(-q)(+q)}{r} + \dfrac{q(-q)}{r\sqrt{2}} + \dfrac{q(-q)}{r\sqrt{2}}\right] \)

\( = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left[\dfrac{q^2}{r} - \dfrac{q^2}{r} + \dfrac{q^2}{r} - \dfrac{q^2}{r} - \dfrac{q^2}{r\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{q^2}{r\sqrt{2}}\right] \)

\( = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left[\dfrac{-2q^2}{r\sqrt{2}}\right] = \left[\dfrac{-\sqrt{2}\,q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r}\right] \)

subtopic: Potential Energy of Charges and Dipoles
stem: Two charged particles having equal charge of \( 3 \times 10^{-5} \) C each are brought from infinity to a separation of 30 cm. Find the increase in electrostatic potential energy during the process.
solution:
Taking the potential energy (PE) at \( \infty \) to be zero,
Increase in PE \( = \) present PE

\( V = \dfrac{q_1 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r} = \dfrac{9 \times 10^{9} \times (3 \times 10^{-5})^2}{0.3} \)

\( = \dfrac{9 \times 9 \times 10^{9} \times 10^{-10}}{3 \times 10^{-1}} = \dfrac{81}{3} = 27 \) J

subtopic: Potential Energy of Charges and Dipoles
stem:
a) Determine the electrostatic potential energy of a system consisting of two charges \( -2\,\mu\text{C} \) and \( +4\,\mu\text{C} \) (with no external field) placed at \( (-8 \) cm, 0, 0) and \( (+8 \) cm, 0, 0) respectively.
b) Suppose the same system of charges is now placed in an external electric field \( E = A\,(1/r^2) \), where \( A = 8 \times 10^{5} \) cm\( ^{-2} \), what would be the electrostatic potential energy of the configuration
solution:
Given :
\( q_1 = -2\,\mu\text{C} = -2 \times 10^{-6} \) C, \( r_1 = 0.08 \) cm
\( q_2 = +4\,\mu\text{C} = +4 \times 10^{-6} \) C, \( r_2 = 0.08 \) cm
\( r = 16 \) cm \( = 0.16 \) m

a) Electrostatic potential energy of the system of two charges is

\( V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{q_1 q_2}{r} \)

\( = \dfrac{9 \times 10^{9} \times (-2) \times 10^{-6} \times 4 \times 10^{-6}}{0.16} \)

\( = 0.45 \) J

b) In the electric field, total potential energy

\( (\text{PE}) = \dfrac{q_1 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r} + q_1 V(\vec{r_1}) + q_2 V(\vec{r_2}) \)

\( E = \dfrac{-dV}{dr} \therefore V = \int -E\,dr = \int \dfrac{-A}{r^2}\,dr,\ V = \dfrac{A}{r} \)

\( \therefore \text{Total PE} = \dfrac{q_1 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r} + \dfrac{A q_1}{r_1} + \dfrac{A q_2}{r_2} \)

\( = -0.45 + \dfrac{8 \times 10^{5} \times (-2 \times 10^{-6})}{0.08} + \dfrac{8 \times 10^{5} \times (4 \times 10^{-6})}{0.08} \)

\( = -0.45 - 20 + 40 \)

\( = 19.55 \) J

subtopic: Potential Energy of Charges and Dipoles
stem:
An electric dipole consists of two opposite charges each of magnitude \( 1\,\mu\text{C} \) separated by 2 cm. The dipole is placed in an external electric field of \( 10^{5} \) N C\( ^{-1} \).
Find:
(i) The maximum torque exerted by the field on the dipole
(ii) The work the external agent will have to do in turning the dipole through \( 180^\circ \) starting from the position \( \theta = 0^\circ \)
solution:
Given :
\( p = q \times 2l = 10^{-6} \times 2 \times 10^{-2} = 2 \times 10^{-8} \) cm
\( E = 10^{5} \) NC\( ^{-1} \)

(i) \( \tau_{\max} = p\,E \sin 90^\circ = 2 \times 10^{-8} \times 10^{5} \times 1 \)
\( = 2 \times 10^{-3} \) Nm

(ii) \( W = pE(\cos\theta_1 - \cos\theta_2) \)
\( = 2 \times 10^{-8} \times 10^{5} \times (\cos 0 - \cos 180^\circ) \)
\( = 2 \times 10^{-3}(1 + 1) = 4 \times 10^{-3} \) J

stem: When \( 10^{8} \) electrons are transferred from one conductor to another, a potential difference of 10 \( V \) appears between the conductors. Find the capacitance of the two conductors.
solution:
Given :
Number of electrons \( n = 10^{8} \)
\( V = 10 \) volt

\( \therefore \) charge transferred
\( Q = ne = 10^{8} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \)
\( (\because e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \) C)
\( = 1.6 \times 10^{-11} \) C

\( \therefore \) Capacitance between two conductors
\( C = \dfrac{Q}{V} = \dfrac{1.6 \times 10^{-11}}{10} = 1.6 \times 10^{-12} \) F

stem: From the figure given below find the value of the capacitance \( C \) if the equivalent capacitance between A and B is to be \( 1\,\mu\text{F} \). All other capacitors are in micro farad.
solution:
Given :
\( C_1 = 8\,\mu\text{F} \), \( C_2 = 4\,\mu\text{F} \), \( C_3 = 1\,\mu\text{F} \), \( C_4 = 4\,\mu\text{F} \), \( C_5 = 4\,\mu\text{F} \)

The effective capacitance of \( C_4 \) and \( C_5 \) in parallel
\( = C_4 + C_5 = 4 + 4 = 8\,\mu\text{F} \)

The effective capacitance of \( C_3 \) and \( 8\,\mu\text{F} \) in series
\( = \dfrac{1 \times 8}{1 + 8} = \dfrac{8}{9}\,\mu\text{F} \)

The capacitance \( 8\,\mu\text{F} \) is in parallel with the series combination of \( C_1 \) and \( C_2 \). Their effective combination is

\( \dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} + \dfrac{8}{9} \Rightarrow \dfrac{8 \times 4}{12} + \dfrac{8}{9} \Rightarrow \dfrac{32}{9}\,\mu\text{F} \)

This capacitance of \( \dfrac{32}{9}\,\mu\text{F} \) is in series with \( C \) and their effective capacitance is given to be \( 1\,\mu\text{F} \)

\( \dfrac{\dfrac{32}{9} \times C}{\dfrac{32}{9} + C} = 1 \)

\( \therefore \dfrac{32}{9} \times C = \dfrac{32}{9} + C \)

\( = 1.392\,\mu\text{F} \)

subtopic: Parallel Plate Capacitor with a Dielectric
stem:
A parallel plate capacitor has an area of 4 cm\( ^2 \) and a plate separation of 2 mm
(i) Calculate its capacitance
(ii) What is its capacitance if the space between the plates is filled completely with a dielectric having dielectric constant of constant 6.7.
solution:
Given
\( A = 4 \) cm\( ^2 = 4 \times 10^{-4} \) m\( ^2 \)
\( d = 2 \) mm \( = 2 \times 10^{-3} \) m
\( \varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \) C\( ^2 \) / Nm\( ^2 \)

(i) Capacitance \( C = \dfrac{A\varepsilon_0}{d} \)
\( = \dfrac{8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 4 \times 10^{-4}}{2 \times 10^{-3}} = 1.77 \times 10^{-12} \) F

(ii) Capacitance \( C' = \dfrac{A\varepsilon_0 k}{d} \)
\( = \dfrac{8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 4 \times 10^{-4} \times 6.7}{2 \times 10^{-3}} \)
\( = 11.86 \times 10^{-12} \) F

subtopic: Parallel Plate Capacitor with a Dielectric
stem: In a capacitor of capacitance \( 20\,\mu\text{F} \), the distance between the plates is 2 mm. If a dielectric slab of width 1 mm and dielectric constant 2 is inserted between the plates, what is the new capacitance?
solution:
Given
\( C = 20\,\mu\text{F} = 20 \times 10^{-6} \) F
\( d = 2 \) mm \( = 2 \times 10^{-3} \) m
\( t = 1 \times 10^{-3} \) m
\( k = 2 \)

\( C = \dfrac{A\varepsilon_0}{d} \) and \( C' = \dfrac{A\varepsilon_0}{d - t + \dfrac{t}{k}} \)

\( \Rightarrow \dfrac{C}{C'} = \dfrac{d - t + \dfrac{t}{k}}{d} \)

\( \Rightarrow \dfrac{20}{C'} = \dfrac{\left(2 \times 10^{-3} - 1 \times 10^{-3} + \dfrac{1 \times 10^{-3}}{2}\right)}{2 \times 10^{-3}} \)

\( \Rightarrow C' = 26.67\,\mu\text{F} \)

stem: A parallel plate air capacitor has a capacitance of \( 3 \times 10^{-9} \) Farad. A slab of dielectric constant 3 and thickness 3 cm completely fills the space between the plates. The potential difference between the plates is maintained constant at 400 volt. What is the change in the energy of capacitor if the slab is removed?
solution:
Energy stored in the capacitor with air

\( E_a = \dfrac{1}{2}CV^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 10^{-9} \times (400)^2 \)
\( = 24 \times 10^{-5} \) J

when the slab of dielectric constant 3 is introduced between the plates of the capacitor, the capacitance of the capacitor increases to
\( C' = kC \)
\( C' = 3 \times 3 \times 10^{-9} = 9 \times 10^{-9} \) F

Energy stored in the capacitor with the dielectric \( (E_d) \)

\( E_d = \dfrac{1}{2}C'V^2 \)

\( E_d = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 10^{-9} \times (400)^2 \)
\( = 72 \times 10^{-5} \) J

Change in energy \( = E_d - E_a = (72 - 24) \times 10^{-5} \)
\( = 48 \times 10^{-5} \) J

There is, therefore, an increase in the energy on introducing the slab of dielectric material.
